{"concepts_used":["GC-0097","GC-0116","GC-0117","GC-0046","GC-0044","GC-0040","GC-0156","GC-0098","GC-0153","GC-0128"],"decline_reason":"","declined":false,"citations":[{"ref":"TMA1995/s224","quote":"(2) If, because of: (a) an error or omission by the person concerned or by his or her agent; or (b) circumstances beyond the control of the person concerned; a relevant act that is required by this Act to be done within a certain time is not, or cannot be, done within that time, the Registrar may, on application made by the person concerned in accordance with the regulations, extend the time for doing the act."},{"ref":"TMR1995/r21.25","quote":"an application for an extension of time for doing a relevant act: (a) must be in an approved form; and (b) must be accompanied by a declaration stating: (i) the facts on which the grounds specified in the application are based; and (ii) if the period for doing the relevant act has ended—the reason why the application was not made before the period ended."},{"ref":"TMM/Part49/2/2/3/2","quote":"The application for an extension of time to file a notice of intention to oppose or a statement of grounds and particulars must be filed with the Trade Marks Office in an approved form and accompanied by the relevant fee (see item 6 in Schedule 9 of the Trade Marks Regulations 1995). The application will not be processed until the fee is paid."},{"ref":"TMM/Part49/2/2/3/2","quote":"The Registrar will give a copy of the extension request to the applicant."},{"ref":"TMA1995/s224(6)","quote":"(6) A person may, as prescribed, oppose the granting of the application."},{"ref":"TMM/Part15/6/6/2","quote":"A notice of opposition to an extension of time under subsection 224(6) must be made in an approved form within one month (not extendible, see paragraph 21.28(2)(b)) of the date of publication (reg 21.20B). The relevant fee must also be paid with the notice of opposition. The Registrar will give a copy of the notice to the extension applicant (subreg 21.20B(2))."},{"ref":"TMM/Part55/3/3/4","quote":"A late application for an award of costs, or a bill of costs that has been filed outside the time limit under reg 21.12, can only be considered if the person concerned is granted an extension of time under s 224. Such an application for extension must be in an approved form and must be filed together with the appropriate fee and a supporting declaration (reg 21.25)."},{"ref":"TMM/Part51/2#1~1","quote":"Absent exceptional circumstances, parties must show that they have made all reasonable efforts to comply with all filing requirements, and that they have acted promptly and diligently at all times to ensure the evidence is filed within the period."},{"ref":"TMM/Part15/1/1/1","quote":"If the delay occurs when the application is within the prescribed 15 month period the examiner will indicate to the applicant that they may make a request close to the lapsing date for an extension of time equivalent to the delay. The Registrar may give consideration to such a request but note that approval of a free extension of time will not be the automatic result of any delay."},{"ref":"TMA1995/s224","quote":"(1) The Registrar must extend the time for doing a relevant act that is required by this Act to be done within a certain time if the act is not, or cannot be, done within that time because of an error or omission by: (a) the Registrar or a Deputy Registrar; or (b) an employee; or (c) a person providing, or proposing to provide, services for the benefit of the Trade Marks Office."},{"ref":"TMM/Part15/6/6/4","quote":"If opposition is filed to the application for extension of time, the procedures for filing evidence and providing for the parties to be heard are determined by the Registrar (see above)."},{"ref":"TMM/Part15/x-relevant-legislation13#1","quote":"Section 223 Fees Section 224 Extension of time The Regulations Reg 4.12 Periods after which applications lapse Reg 21.4 Filing of documents - treatment of non-complying documents"}],"answer":"The supplied passages identify the following affected people and roles. This is not a complete account of the scope of every provision listed in the Manual’s legislation index.

- **People seeking extensions of time, including where their agents have made errors.** Under the **Act**, s 224(2) permits the Registrar, on a compliant application, to extend time where the person’s or their agent’s error or omission, or circumstances beyond the person’s control, prevented timely performance. Under the **Regulations**, r 21.25 requires an approved form and supporting declaration, including an explanation for a late extension application. [1–2]

- **Potential opponents and the trade mark applicants affected by their requests.** The **Manual practice** for extensions to file a notice of intention to oppose or statement of grounds and particulars requires an approved-form application and relevant fee; processing waits until payment. The Registrar sends the request to the trade mark applicant. [3–4]

- **People opposing an extension, and the extension applicant.** The **Act**, s 224(6), allows a person to oppose as prescribed. The **Manual practice** requires the opposition notice within one month of publication, describes that period as not extendible, requires payment of the fee with the notice, and provides for a copy to the extension applicant. [5–6]

- **People filing late costs applications or bills of costs.** The **Manual practice** says these can only be considered if an extension under s 224 is granted; the extension application must include the approved form, appropriate fee and supporting declaration. [7]

- **Parties filing opposition evidence.** The **Manual practice** says that, absent exceptional circumstances, they must demonstrate all reasonable efforts to comply with filing requirements and prompt, diligent conduct throughout. [8]

- **Trade mark applicants approaching lapsing after an examination delay.** The **Manual practice** describes requesting an extension equivalent to the delay close to the lapsing date, but expressly says a free extension is not automatic. [9]

- **The Registrar and Office personnel.** The **Act**, s 224(1), requires the Registrar to extend time where the specified failure results from an error or omission by the Registrar, Deputy Registrar, an employee or a relevant service provider. The **Manual practice** also assigns the Registrar responsibility for determining evidence and hearing procedures when an extension is opposed. [10–11]

**Limit:** The supplied index names s 223 (fees), r 4.12 (lapsing) and r 21.4 (non-complying documents), but does not reproduce their operative provisions. I therefore cannot establish their full scope, or everyone affected by those general rules, from these passages alone. [12]"}
